kildare and leighlin dioceseand and day of prayer for survivors and victims of abuse friday february 20th 2026 (1st friday of lent 2026) - our annual holy hour for survivors of abuse was held in the cathedral parish in carlow. thanks to all who attended and participated in the service. candle of atonement prayer lord, forgive us our many sins. we grieve and repent with all our hearts for having offended you, for our great failings and neglect of the young and vulnerable. we place all of those who have been hurt by the church in any way into your loving hands and under the protection of our blessed mother. lord, bring peace to their broken lives and show us all the way out of darkness and into the light of your word. may we as the people of god be more fully human, more fully christ-like and more fully your people, that we may see the errors of the past and go forward with renewed hope and faith in christ and in our church. amen. testimonials from young people who engage in youth activities in our diocese. message from bishop denis nulty sunday, february 22, is diocesan safeguarding sunday. it is the first sunday of lent and appropriately so, as we enter the penitential season and seek forgiveness for past failings. in his address at the january consistory pope leo xiv reminded all that “abuse itself causes a deep wound, which may last a lifetime; but often the scandal in the church is that the door was closed and victims were not welcomed or accompanied with the closeness of authentic pastors”. this year we have intentionally linked the ‘day of prayer for survivors and victims of abuse’ on friday, february 20 with ‘safeguarding sunday’ two days later. the national child safeguarding policy for our church is called ‘a safe and welcoming church’ and that is what our diocese is and our parishes are, a safe and welcoming church. the fact that ‘safeguarding sunday’ has become such a regular part of our diocesan and parish life, demonstrates how the safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults has been so well embedded into every area of the life of our diocese, its 56 parishes and 117 faith communities. safeguarding sunday is once again an opportunity to acknowledge and recognise the years of dedication and work by so many to ensure that kildare & leighlin diocese is a safe place for children and all who work with them. it’s an opportunity to thank all who today ensure safeguarding is so well embedded in our diocesan culture, ailish higgins, our director of safeguarding, currently on maternity leave, michele hughes, our acting designated liaison person, the diocesan safeguarding committee, our parish safeguarding representatives, our priests, our deacons and our people, particularly the many who volunteer at parish level, ensuring the life and vitality of their faith community. as ever, on my parish visits, i encourage ministry with children and young people, this is an essential part of the mission of the church. where altar serving, youth choirs, sunday school have returned i welcome them warmly; where they haven’t for whatever reason, once again i encourage their early return. the life of a parish is often defined by the active engagement of young people in that parish. safeguarding sunday is a reassurance to all that being involved in the parish is governed by best practices in safeguarding. every blessing & thanks, bishop of kildare and leighlin +denis nulty if you have a safeguarding concern, please contact: diocesan designated liaison person (dlp): ailish higgins tel:
